sections.html:
Caroline County is in eastern Virginia, with the Rappahannock River along its north edge. It is about 30 miles north of Richmond and 32 miles south of Fredericksburg, so a lot of residents drive out for work along Interstate 95, which crosses the county at exits 104 and 110. The county covers 537 square miles and had 30,887 residents in 2020. Bowling Green is the seat and the largest town, and Port Royal is the only other incorporated town.

Many homes are fairly recent additions to an older farming landscape, since the population is roughly double what it was fifty years earlier. Buyers ask about the commute first, and houses near an I-95 exit are usually easier to describe than ones at the end of a long rural road.

Real estate tax is due June 5 and December 5. Both a 10 percent penalty and 10 percent interest are added on June 6 and December 6, and that covers real estate, personal property and business personal property.

Bill or feeDue date
First installmentJune 5
Second installmentDecember 5
Penalty and interest10 percent each, added the next day
Water bills15 days from the billing date
Dog tagJanuary 31
Business licenseMarch 1

Virginia sets the ceiling. Code of Virginia 58.1-3916 allows interest up to 10 percent a year and a penalty up to 10 percent of the past-due property tax. A locality may waive both when the failure was not the taxpayer's fault, or when a payment was mailed on time with proof of mailing and arrived within five days of the deadline.

sections.h2: Treasurer and Commissioner of the Revenue contacts
sections.html:
The Treasurer collects the tax and the Commissioner of the Revenue answers assessment questions. They are separate offices.

  • Treasurer: 212 N Main Street, Bowling Green, VA 22427. Mail goes to P.O. Box 431. Phone 804-633-5291, Monday through Friday, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.
  • Real estate questions at the Commissioner's office: 804-633-9834 or realestate@co.caroline.va.us.
  • General county mail: P.O. Box 447, Bowling Green, VA 22427.

The Treasurer takes payment online, by phone through ACI, by mail, in person or by monthly automatic withdrawal. A drop box in front of the County Administration Building handles after-hours payments. The county guarantees only payments made through its own website and Official Payments, so a payment sent through a personal bank bill-pay service is at your risk.

sections.h2: How to check or appeal your assessment
sections.html:
Start with the county's online Real Estate Assessment Information tool at caroline.civ.quest and the Tax Map page that shows parcels, then call the Commissioner's real estate office. If you still disagree after a reassessment, the next stop is the Board of Equalization.

The county lays out the path this way. Owners with concerns about a reassessment first go to hearings with the Board of Assessors. A Board of Equalization is then set up to review complaints: a six-member citizen panel, nominated by the Board of Supervisors and approved by a Circuit Court judge in each general reassessment year, whose members complete Virginia Department of Taxation training. After the board finishes, the only option left is a petition to the Circuit Court under Section 58.1-3984.

State law helps you prepare. Under 58.1-3379 the assessor's value is presumed correct, and the owner must show it is above fair market value, applied unevenly, or not set under accepted appraisal practice. For a residential property with fewer than four units, the assessing officer has 15 days to hand over the assessment records after a written request.

sections.h2: Permits, land use and utilities before you sell
sections.html:
Four local items come up most: building permits, land use programs, utilities and the recording cost at closing. Each has its own office, so confirm them early.

  • Building permits: any new building, renovation, addition or major improvement needs a permit, plus plumbing and mechanical permits. A certificate of occupancy follows satisfactory completion. Building Inspections is at 804-633-4303. Sort out unpermitted work before you list.
  • Land use: the Commissioner of the Revenue runs the land preservation program and rechecks each enrolled property every year. Ask that office whether your parcel is enrolled and what rollback would apply.
  • Utilities: the county names the Carmel Church Ladysmith, Milford, Port Royal and Townfield water systems. Public Utilities is at 804-633-4390.
  • Relief for older and disabled owners: call the real estate office at 804-633-9834.

At closing, the grantor tax under Virginia 58.1-802 is fifty cents on every $500 of value. The statute names the seller as payer, though the two sides can agree to split it differently.

Back taxes mean stacked penalty and interest and a bigger payoff at closing. Since the county adds both charges the day after each due date, a missed December 5 bill grows right away.

Ask the Treasurer for the balance as of your expected closing day, and have the closing agent confirm it. When a house needs more work than a retail buyer will accept, an as-is cash purchase can save repairs and showing time, and the unpaid balance comes out of the proceeds at closing.

Cash Home Buyers can look at a Caroline County house with back taxes and plan around whatever figure the Treasurer gives you.

1. Call the Treasurer at 804-633-5291 for the balance on both installments.
  2. Look up your parcel on caroline.civ.quest and compare the record with the house.
  3. Ask the real estate office at 804-633-9834 about land use or relief.
  4. Confirm any permits are closed out with Building Inspections.
  5. Hand your closing agent the payoff letter and receipts.

faqs.q: When are Caroline County real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: June 5 and December 5. The county adds a 10 percent penalty and 10 percent interest on June 6 and December 6 for real estate and personal property.

faqs.q: Where is the Caroline County Treasurer's office?
faqs.a: At 212 N Main Street in Bowling Green, open weekdays from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. The phone number is 804-633-5291, and the mailing address is P.O. Box 431, Bowling Green, VA 22427.

faqs.q: How do I appeal a Caroline County real estate assessment?
faqs.a: Talk to the Commissioner of the Revenue's real estate office first, then go to the Board of Equalization if you still disagree. After that, the only remaining step is a Circuit Court petition under Section 58.1-3984 of the Code of Virginia.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Caroline County house if I owe back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, in most cases the balance is paid from the sale proceeds at closing. Ask the Treasurer for a current payoff figure and have your closing agent confirm it.

faqs.q: Who pays the Virginia grantor tax when a Caroline County house sells?
faqs.a: The statute puts the grantor tax of fifty cents per $500 on the seller, but buyer and seller may agree that the buyer pays some or all of it.
